claims.text: As-cast HfMoTaTiZr has a density of approximately 10.21 g/cm³.
As-cast HfMoTaTiZr has a room-temperature yield strength of approximately 1600 MPa.
As-cast HfMoTaTiZr has an elevated-temperature yield strength of approximately 855 MPa.
Replacing 10–20% of the Hf content with Al is the proposed compositional intervention.
Partial replacement of Hf by Al will reduce the density of HfMoTaTiZr.
Partial replacement of Hf by Al will not substantially compromise room-temperature strength.
Partial replacement of Hf by Al will not substantially compromise strength at approximately 1000 °C.
The Al-modified alloy will form a dual-phase microstructure consisting of a continuous disordered BCC matrix and discrete ordered precipitates.
The ordered precipitates in the Al-modified alloy will be coherent or semi-coherent with the BCC matrix.
Al chemical interactions with the refractory elements will promote ordered intermetallic precipitation within a disordered BCC matrix.
The ordered precipitates will impede dislocation motion and provide precipitation strengthening.
An inverted microstructure with a continuous disordered BCC matrix and discrete B2 precipitates has been observed in another Al-containing RHEA.
The precipitation-strengthening mechanism is expected to preserve high yield strength at both ambient and elevated temperatures.
The Al substitution should reduce density by approximately 5–10%, with a target density below 9.5 g/cm³.
The Al-modified alloy should retain a room-temperature yield strength near 1600 MPa.
The Al-modified alloy should retain a yield strength around 850 MPa at approximately 1000 °C.
Mechanical comparison should be conducted from approximately 25 °C to 1000 °C at a strain rate near 1×10⁻³ s⁻¹.
The stability and morphology of the proposed ordered precipitates after Al substitution are uncertain.

contradictions.description: The intervention describes replacing 10–20 atomic % of Hf, which can mean 10–20 percentage points of the whole alloy, whereas the experiment describes replacing 10% or 20% of the Hf content, corresponding to only 2 or 4 atomic % Al for equiatomic HfMoTaTiZr.
The example formula AlxMoTaTiZr omits Hf entirely, conflicting with the stated partial substitution of Hf and with the proposed 10% and 20% replacement series.
A 5% reduction from 10.21 g/cm³ corresponds to about 9.70 g/cm³, not the stated target below 9.5 g/cm³; the latter requires a reduction of about 7%.
